knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The guide says cloth-type masks give almost no protection and sit outside regulation. The other options are regulated, fluid-resistant or respirator types.
The guide wants the apron fastened at the rear with the tie behind the neck, since a knot at the front can get soiled and carry contamination.
The guide says masks are changed between clients and discarded at once if wet. Appearance is not a reliable test of a used mask.

practicalCriteria: Given a task with a listed fluid risk, the learner selects the gown or apron, mask, eye protection and gloves the facility lists, and states the size check.
The learner fastens an apron at the rear and changes a mask between two simulated clients without prompts.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation of the selection and change sequence
Fit-test record for any respirator used in the assessment
stopWorkCriteria: A glove, gown, apron or mask is torn, soiled or wet during a task: stop, replace it, and clean hands before continuing.
A respirator is needed but no fit-test record exists: stop and refer to the supervisor.
